advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a distinct `outcome_counts` bucket (e.g. `degraded`) for the non-contract honest-degrade `except Exception` branch so telemetry covers every chunk outcome.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:332: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — a non-contract failure (network/etc.) → honest degrade`
Commit message: 'Add outcome_counts telemetry ... so callers can see per-chunk verification health'; the honest-degrade outcome class is not one of clean/recovered/empty_outcomes/unrecoverable
ABSENCE: no test exercises the honest-degrade branch's effect on outcome_counts (tests cover clean/empty/recovered/shape-failure only, test_review_kernel.py:415-533)
advisory.finding: The non-contract honest-degrade path (`except Exception`) increments none of the four `outcome_counts` buckets, so a chunk that fails on a network/etc. error is completely invisible in the telemetry — contradicting the docstring/commit framing of 'per-chunk verification health' and leaving sum(outcome_counts.values()) < number of chunks whenever a degrade occurs.
scenarios: A verifier chunk fails with a transient network error rather than a StructuredOutputError
An operator reading outcome_counts to gauge run health sees counts that silently under-report total chunks

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Only count `recovered` when the per-chunk reshape actually produced at least one merged verification (else classify as empty/unrecoverable).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:199-200: `has_violations` is true when `malformed or duplicates or unexpected` — including cases where the merged map is empty
src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:242: only valid, in-range, non-malformed items populate `merged`
advisory.finding: A chunk whose non-empty raw_output contains only malformed and/or out-of-range (`unexpected`) items — so nothing is merged into the verification map — is still tallied as `recovered`, overstating that anything was actually recovered.
scenarios: Verifier returns a non-empty list of items all with non-int or out-of-range indices

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider deriving the clean/recovered classification without a second full reshape pass (e.g. reshape once and inspect per-chunk).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/verify.py:348-350: global `reshape = reshape_verifications([v for out in chunk_outputs for v in out], valid_indices=sent_indices)`
advisory.finding: `reshape_verifications` is now invoked twice per non-empty chunk — once per-chunk solely to compute the clean/recovered classification (line 343) and again globally over the concatenated outputs (line 348) — a redundant recompute of the same tolerant merge.
scenarios: Every non-empty chunk on every verify run

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where `run_chunk` raises a non-StructuredOutputError exception and assert `outcome_counts` stays all-zero and `contract_violations` has no `empty_outcomes` key.
evidence: verify.py:332-334: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 ... chunk_outputs.append([]) / continue` — the added `continue` skips the empty_outcome_indices detection at lines 336-341

The four new tests cover clean, empty (returns []), recovered (duplicate), and StructuredOutputError; ABSENCE: none raises a non-StructuredOutputError exception to exercise the honest-degrade path's telemetry (which must increment NO counter and NOT flag empty_outcomes)
advisory.finding: The generic `except Exception` honest-degrade branch (modified by the diff to add a `continue` that now bypasses the empty-check and every `outcome_counts` bucket) has no test. No test asserts that a non-contract failure (network/etc.) leaves all four counters at 0 and, critically, is NOT miscounted as an `empty_outcomes` (its `chunk_outputs.append([])` would look empty if the `continue` regressed).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_verify_findings_honest_degrade_counts_no_outcome` with a `run_chunk` that raises `RuntimeError`; assert `result['outcome_counts'] == {'clean':0,'recovered':0,'empty_outcomes':0,'unrecoverable':0}` and `'empty_outcomes' not in result['contract_violations']`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten the mixed-chunks test to assert `counts['clean'] == 4` and `counts['recovered'] == 0` instead of `>= 1`.
evidence: test_review_kernel.py:508: `findings = [_fnd(f"f{i}") for i in range(6)]` with idx2→empty and idx4→StructuredOutputError, leaving 0,1,3,5 as clean = exactly 4
advisory.finding: The mixed-chunks tally test asserts `counts['clean'] >= 1` where the exact expected value is 4 (indices 0,1,3,5 are clean; idx2 empty, idx4 shape-failure). The loose inequality lets a real miscounting regression (e.g. only counting the first clean chunk) pass, defeating the test's stated purpose that 'one bad chunk's telemetry must not swallow a good chunk's'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `assert counts["clean"] >= 1` with `assert counts["clean"] == 4` and add `assert counts["recovered"] == 0`.
